behavioral_signatures: Discrepancy between declared and actual (deployed) dependencies
Presence of binaries or files not listed in manifest
Manually copied or tampered dependency files
Transitive dependencies not declared in manifest but present in build
file_indicators: Files or binaries present in build output but not referenced in manifest (e.g., .jar, .dll, .so, .pyc, etc.)
Unexpected or duplicate dependency files in build artifacts
Artifacts with structural similarity to known malicious components
network_indicators: Not directly applicable from this report, but in general: unexpected network activity during build or install phase
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Use as-observed (as-deployed) scanning methodologies to enumerate all actual files and dependencies present in the built application or container image, not just those declared in manifest files. Compare the as-declared dependency list (from manifest files like package.json, requirements.txt, pom.xml, etc.) with the as-observed list (from the actual build output or deployed image). Flag any files, binaries, or dependencies present in the as-observed scan but missing from the as-declared manifest for further investigation. Pay special attention to manually copied files, post-build artifacts, and transitive dependencies that are not explicitly declared. Automated tools should alert on any discrepancies, unexpected binaries, or structural similarities to known malicious components.
